description:
Role Purpose

The AI Strategy role identifies, frames, validates, and prioritizes the AI opportunities that offer potential for significant enterprise revenue and margin growth. This individual acts as a organizational thought leader to our company's leadership in order to decide what opportunities to attack, how to attack them, how to prioritize them, and what to initiate, accelerate, or stop ahead of critical investment decisions.

This is a strategy and business-judgment role. It sits with SBU and functional leaders to turn financial, operational, and clinical problems into investment-ready theses: the problem, the customer or clinician, the first principles approach, the opportunity value, the investment required to unlock that value, the risk, and the conditions under which the work should proceed or cease.

This is not a builder role. Solution design, technical feasibility, and build execution sit with AI Business Partners, Product Builders, enterprise architecture, and technology colleagues. AI Strategy owns the quality of the question and the quality of the bet.

Key Responsibilities

Problem Framing & Opportunity Assessment

• Partner with enterprise and SBU, finance, operations, and clinical and pharmacy leaders to identify business problems where AI could create significant, even non-linear, value unlock.

• Frame each opportunity in business terms: who is served, what changes, what value is at stake, what risk is introduced, and what would have to be true for the work to succeed.

• Conduct rigorous qualitative and quantitative user and market research to validate the opportunity in order to derisk the bet.

• Distinguish problems for which AI offers non-linear advantages, (i.e. not just problems that need process, policy, data, or operating-model change), and conduct a first principles decomposition of the problem's points of leverage and AI's ability to unlock value against those points.

• Translate enterprise and SBU challenges into opportunities with measurable financial value, outcomes, and experiential improvements, not a list of use cases.

• Bring a clear recommendation to proceed, sequence, partner, or stop.

Portfolio Strategy & Investment Framing

• Stack-rank opportunities on strategic alignment, customer or clinical value, feasibility (in partnership with product and technology colleagues), risk, cost, and speed to value, developing a robust and rigorous scoring methodology aligned to our organization's strategic needs.

• Develop business cases, investment theses, value realization models, and roadmaps that a business owner have data to stand behind.

• Assess buy, build, partner, and hybrid paths as business choices, and flag duplicate investment across teams.

• Explore non-traditional investment routes to solving problems, such as exploration of venture investment, incubation, or even M&A discussion, alongside colleagues from these areas.

• Define success metrics and measurement instrumentation before work is staffed, including adoption, productivity, financial impact, quality, customer experience, and clinical outcomes.

• Revisit the AI portfolio as evidence arrives, and retire or reframe work that is not earning the next increment of investment, seeking to drive an "innovation rate of return" on the total body of work.

• Establish stage-gates and evidence expectations for concept, pilot, and broader adoption decisions.

title: Sr. Global Alliance Director, OEM, Storage and ISV
description:
As Sr. Global Alliance Director at vCluster Labs , you aren’t just shipping integrations; you are deciding which stack the world’s AI factories get built out of. Every AI factory ships as a stack: servers from an OEM, a validated design, a scheduler, an observability layer, a data platform, a management plane. The tenant isolation layer is the part nobody has solved. Your job is to make sure that layer is already in the OEM’s reference architecture, already in the price book, and already integrated with the ISVs sitting next to us before the customer ever runs a bake-off. Being in the design is worth more than winning the deal, because you win every deal that design produces.
This is a founding, zero-to-one role on a first-year partner program. There is no partner channel to inherit and no team underneath you. You own the number, the agreements behind it, and the product that ships inside someone else’s box.
As Sr. Global Alliance Director your role will include:

• Owning the OEM alliance strategy: You will own the server and systems vendors building validated AI infrastructure designs end to end: strategy, executive alignment, program agreements, and business reviews. You will design and stand up the OEM commercial model (embedded SKUs, unit economics, tiered pricing for bundled and embedded distribution, royalty and per-node constructs, and a standard OEM order template that lets legal review once and the field move fast), then negotiate and close the orders. You will monitor each OEM’s AI factory roadmap to spot the design cycle before it closes, not after.

• Building the ISV portfolio: You will scope, prioritize, and drive integrations with the storage, network, scheduler, observability, security, data, MLOps, and inference vendors whose customers overlap with ours, running it as a portfolio with explicit thresholds, not a queue of requests. You will land vCluster inside ISV and SaaS platforms as the tenant isolation layer, whether the ISV embeds it, resells it, or co-sells it. You will kill integrations that will not produce, and say so early. An ISV embed that does not change the partner’s own roadmap is a logo, not a route.

• Building the sell-with motion: A shipped integration with no joint motion behind it is a cost, not an asset. You will design repeatable co-sell plays on top of every integration that earns one (account mapping, joint solution briefs, field-to-field engagement, deal registration the partner’s sellers actually use), then connect the resulting opportunities to vCluster’s regional sellers, channel partners, and the NVIDIA alliance to close. You take bundles to market through the partner’s own sales motion, not around it.

• Driving technical alignment on both sides: You will represent partner technology requirements inside vCluster Product and Engineering with evidence attached (which accounts, what revenue, what happens if we do nothing), through one front door: licensing, telemetry, air-gapped operation, support boundaries, and lifecycle. You will write the integration specifications and acceptance criteria yourself. Integration work fails on unclear criteria far more often than on technical difficulty, and that clarity is yours to own.

• Building the technology alliance program: You will design and launch the program itself: tiers, technical certification requirements, joint solution briefs, marketplace and private offer paths, and a self-serve path so a small ISV can integrate without you in the loop. The program has to scale past the partners you personally manage.

• Owning the partnership number: You will report partner-influenced pipeline, integration and certification milestones, joint bookings contribution, and field activation to vCluster leadership, with MEDDPICC on every joint opportunity and weekly pipeline inspection. This is a first-year partner program with team MBOs and OKRs; you show up to the weekly inspection with your own numbers, your own forecast, and your own plan to close

Ad Age recently described us as "if Omnicom was rebuilt on AI." Your job is to turn a line like that into an argument the market repeats back to us. The split is roughly 80% Darkroom, 20% Shadow.

We are making a category bet on the forward-deployed marketer, the operator who sits inside a business and builds with AI rather than briefing the work out. We intend to make that a term of art through Darkroom: the article, the LinkedIn engine, the video, the webinars, the press. You own that campaign end to end.

You'll report to our VP of Marketing, who sets direction and makes the calls. You'll help shape the thinking behind it: how content maps to the funnel, which channels carry which offers, and what actually turns attention into pipeline. Then you build the content that proves it.

Our marketing operations manager owns the calendar, the publishing, and the deployment. You make the content that fills all of it, across LinkedIn, video, email, paid, and creator, and you brief our designer, video editor, and SEO specialist so one idea becomes a post, a video, an email, and an ad in the same week. This isn't a writing-only role.

Alongside content, you own the creative half of the creator program: who we work with, what we ask them to make, and the call on whether we go wide with many creators or deep with a few. You source and negotiate the partnerships and write the briefs. Marketing Ops runs the admin behind it. Creator content is one of our two strongest lead sources today and the one with the most room left in it.

This is a New York-based role operating in the EST Time Zone, hybrid out of our new NYC office, and all business is conducted 100% in English.

- Shadow Content: Take Shadow's content from scattered to a funnel: posts into webinars and lead magnets into signups. Product marketing for a platform that sells to operators.

- Paid Copy: Partner with our designer, video editor and performance team on the words behind our ads, so the organic and creator assets that work become the ads that work.
